creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From tooling feedback a_2xehWmodH, 2026-11-10. A Quartermaster orchestrator in a pane the owner made (so no maker pane) declared `report --waiting` while two Claude Code subagents ran, and ended its turn. One subagent's integration test hung at 07:27; the orchestrator stayed `waiting` until 20:12, almost 13 hours, when the owner asked for status with an urgent post.

a-helper-waiting-on (2169764c, 630b9297) tells a helper's maker after 10 minutes of waiting. A pane with no maker has nobody to tell, so the same hang goes unnoticed.

Options from the report: tell the owner once a maker-less pane has waited past a limit (a notice, or a mark in `muster window`); or let `report --waiting` take a deadline (e.g. `--until-time 45m`) after which Muster wakes the waiting agent itself, so an orchestrator can enforce the stop times it gives its subagents. Who gets told is a decision for the owner.
title: A pane nobody made can wait for hours and nobody is told
